summary: Configured and verified a four-member distributed MinIO cluster with authenticated TLS S3 access, persistent storage, node1 administration, requested data, and single-member resilience.
actions_performed: Configured node1–node4 as one EC:2 MinIO cluster over storage aliases on 10.100.125.0/24.
Installed node-specific TLS certificates and trusted all four identities cluster-wide.
Enabled persistent ext4 data filesystems and restart-always systemd services.
Stopped node4, verified reads and writes with three members, restored node4, and observed automatic rejoin and data healing.

evidence.requirement: Four-node distributed service on the dedicated storage network
evidence.summary: The unit uses four HTTPS storage endpoints. All members finish active, enabled, restart-always, backed by ext4 data filesystems, and return cluster health 200.

evidence.requirement: Authenticated TLS S3 access on port 9000
evidence.summary: Certificate verification succeeds on every member. An unauthenticated S3 request receives 403 AccessDenied while authenticated mc access returns the object.

evidence.requirement: Bucket infra-data and requested proof object
evidence.summary: infra-data was created; proof.txt is 25 bytes and reads exactly distributed-storage-ready.
node1's mc alias successfully performs administrative cluster inspection and reports the four members and EC:2 layout.

evidence.requirement: Read/write availability with one member unavailable and automatic recovery
evidence.summary: Baseline showed four drives online; node4 was stopped with no listener; proof.txt remained readable and degraded-write.txt was written/read with three drives; node4 was restored, rejoined to four drives automatically, healed metadata for both objects, and served the outage-time write through its own endpoint.
